home.aboutText1: I am a visual artist and tattoo artist, and my work moves between drawing, painting, and ceramics. Through my creations, I explore the relationship between the body, nature, and human sensitivity. My work is strongly influenced by ecofeminism, the connection with the environment, and the emotions that permeate us. As a tattoo artist, I specialize in delicate designs with an organic and fluid aesthetic, often inspired by natural elements such as flowers and plants.
home.aboutText2: For many of my clients, getting a tattoo is a symbolic act, a gesture of transformation or personal resignification, and I love being able to accompany them in this process. In my painting and ceramic work, I also explore the connection between the human and the natural, creating images and objects that evoke strength, tenderness, and harmony with the world around us. Each piece I create, whether a tattoo, a painting, or a ceramic piece, is a dialogue between my artistic universe and those who inhabit it.
home.aboutArtistSubtitle: My work is born from a sense of discomfort: the feeling of being disconnected from nature and, at the same time, from my own body. I work from that place of tension, exploring how cultural systems—patriarchy, capitalism, and urban life—shape our perception of the natural, the feminine, and the instinctive. Through painting, sculpture, and tattooing, I develop images where the female body merges with, resists, or transforms in relation to its environment. I am interested in representing non-hegemonic bodies, vulnerable yet powerful; bodies that escape domestication and approach the wild as a form of freedom. My practice is deeply influenced by ecofeminism, understanding the connection between the exploitation of nature and the oppression of feminized bodies. At this crossroads, questions about belonging, identity, and memory emerge: what does it mean to return to nature when we have been historically separated from it? Water, earth, animals, and landscapes function as symbols of transformation, loss, and resistance. In them, I project both contemporary anxiety and the possibility of reconnection. My work does not seek to provide answers, but to open spaces for reflection on how we inhabit our bodies and the world.

tattoos.book: Send your idea via the contact form with references and size/placement. I'll reply with availability, an estimate, and the next steps. A deposit may be required to secure a date.
tattoos.pain: Pain varies by person and body area. I work gently, take breaks when needed, and provide aftercare instructions to ensure a smooth healing process.
tattoos.prepare: Sleep well, stay hydrated, and eat before your session. Avoid alcohol and blood thinners 24 hours prior. Wear comfortable clothing that provides easy access to the area.

ceramics.custom: Yes. Share your idea, function, measurements, and preferred finish. I'll confirm feasibility and an estimated timeline before starting.
ceramics.timeline: Typically 3–6 weeks depending on complexity, drying times, glazing, and kiln availability.
ceramics.safe: Most functional pieces are dishwasher safe and microwave friendly unless stated otherwise. Sculptural pieces are for display only.

artworks.purchase: Yes, selected works are available. If you're interested in a specific piece or commission, please reach out to discuss availability and pricing.
artworks.prints: Limited edition prints may be available for certain pieces. Ask about current editions and sizes.
artworks.mediums: Primarily oil and acrylic on canvas, watercolor on paper, and mixed media depending on the series.

orders.process: We discuss your idea, timeline, budget, and references. I'll propose a concept and quote. A deposit starts the project; the balance is due upon delivery.
orders.payments: Common digital methods and bank transfers are accepted. Details will be provided during booking.

general.location: Based in Melbourne, Australia. Some projects can be arranged remotely—feel free to ask.
general.reply: I typically respond within 1–3 business days. If it's urgent, mention it in your message.

orders.faq1A: For tattoos, I recommend booking 2-4 weeks in advance. Ceramic pieces take 4-6 weeks, and murals vary depending on scope and size.

biography.title: Biography
biography.description: My journey through art and creativity
biography.bio1: Nicole Teper is an Argentinian visual artist and tattoo artist based in Melbourne. Her interdisciplinary practice includes painting, sculpture, and tattooing, focusing on the relationship between the body, nature, and the systems of power that shape both.
biography.bio2: From an ecofeminist perspective, her work reflects on contemporary disconnection from the natural world and examines how patriarchal and capitalist structures influence subjectivity and territory.
biography.bio3: Her work features non-normative bodies in relation to organic landscapes, animals, and natural elements, creating imagery that moves between the intimate and the political. Through these intersections, she explores themes of identity, memory, transformation, and resistance, offering a critical perspective on how we inhabit both our bodies and our environment.
biography.bio4: She holds a degree in Visual Arts and currently develops her artistic practice alongside her work as a tattoo artist, specializing in botanical color pieces, maintaining an ongoing dialogue between both disciplines.
